final_message:
I fixed the bug. The new test passes along with the rest of the suite (25 tests), and mypy is clean.

**Cause:** `recover()` in `billing/dunning.py` is meant to return a `past_due` or `unpaid` subscription to `active` once its invoice is paid. When no other invoices were outstanding, its body was just `pass`, so the subscription stayed `past_due` after a successful retry.

**Fix:** in that case it now calls `transition(ctx, subscription, "active")`.

I added your reproduction as a new test in `tests/test_dunning_recovery.py`. I also wrote `answer.json` in the repository root:

```json
{"file": "dunning.py", "function": "recover"}
```

steps.command: cd billing && ls && wc -l *.py && grep -n "past_due\|retry\|def " engine.py | head -100; cat ../tests/conftest.py | head -80
cd billing && cat dunning.py payments.py; sed -n 85,110p engine.py

cd .. && python3 - <<'E'
p='billing/dunning.py'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("    if not outstanding:\n        pass","    if not outstanding:\n        transition(ctx, subscription, \"active\")")
open(p,'w').write(s)
E
echo '{"file": "dunning.py", "function": "recover"}' > answer.json
cat >> tests/test_recovery_tmp.py <<'E'
E
rm tests/test_recovery_tmp.py
cat >> tests/test_dunning_recovery.py <<'E'


def test_recovery_after_retry_succeeds(world):
    cus = world.customer()
    world.gateway.fail_next.append("card_declined")
    sub = world.engine.subscribe(cus["id"], [(world.monthly["id"], 1)])
    assert sub["status"] == "past_due"
    world.advance_days(1)
    assert sub["status"] == "active"
    [inv] = world.engine.invoices_for(cus["id"])
    assert inv["status"] == "paid"
E
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -8; .venv/bin/python -m mypy billing | tail -3
